answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using zero-knowledge proof-of-personhood nullifiers. To register, an agent derives a deterministic tag from a signed human credential, splitting private attributes like a prism so verifiers block duplicates without exposing identities. Instead of swarming like a sparrow across open tundra, attackers incur the verifiable cost of securing scarce unique human sponsors per identity. However, adversaries can still rent credentials from paid proxies.
